subject.title: Feature Request: Masked Secrets - Prevent Agent from Accessing Raw API Keys

question: Should OpenClaw implement a native masked-secrets/process-isolation boundary for agent-executed commands, route this through scoped credential-broker/plugin APIs, or explicitly leave it to external OS/plugin isolation?
rationale: The gap is source-proven and security-sensitive, but the fix defines a credential trust boundary and public config/API behavior rather than a narrow bug repair.

options.title: Sponsor a security-owned native design
options.body: Define the credential boundary, dispatch-time injection, exact redaction, migration/docs, and plugin-provider integration before implementation.

options.title: Route through credential-broker/plugin seams
options.body: Keep core lean by prioritizing the missing broker or plugin APIs that let external credential providers cover this safely.

options.title: Declare external hardening the supported path
options.body: Close the core direction only after maintainers explicitly choose OS isolation, external proxies, and ClawHub plugins as the supported answer.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a security-owned native design
recommendation.body: Define the credential boundary, dispatch-time injection, exact redaction, migration/docs, and plugin-provider integration before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice is a security-boundary decision on paths CODEOWNERS routes to the security owner group.
